about: FRISIA AND THE RHINE DELTA, 780-1070: who ruled, and the wars, raids, laws, coins and church events a merchant of Dorestad and his heirs lived under. Written 4 October 2026 for Kapman from the annals (St Bertin, Fulda, Xanten as given at gjallar.nl; Regino; Alpert; the project's own port dossiers) and the Wikipedia pages named in 'sources'. Years are Julian. In 'rulers', 'from' and 'to' are years and a ruler holds until the day told in 'how_ended'. 'line' groups rulers so the game can ask one line for one year and get one name: king (the king or emperor over Dorestad and Utrecht), subking_lotharingia, duke_lotharingia (903-965), duke_lower_lotharingia (from 959), bishop_utrecht, archbishop_cologne, west_frisia (Dorestad, Kennemerland and the mouths of Rhine and Maas: the king's agents, the Danish lords, then the counts later called of Holland), zeeland, middle_frisia, east_frisia, hamaland (Deventer), teisterbant (Tiel). The lines king, bishop_utrecht, archbishop_cologne and west_frisia have no gaps from 787 to 1070; the others have gaps where no name survives, and in a gap the king's line answers. In the year a ruler changes, both names hold that year: the day is in 'how_ended'. 'over' lists port ids from ports_793.json. In 'raids', 'where' is a port id from ports_793.json where the place is one; otherwise the place by name, with 'near' giving the nearest port ids. (?) marks what was not checked against a source on the day. Words are our own; nothing is quoted from a modern translation. Edit freely.

rulers.name: Charles (Charlemagne)
rulers.title: king of the Franks from 768, emperor from 25 December 800
rulers.seat: no fixed seat; Aachen in winter from 794; a palace above the Waal at Nijmegen
rulers.note: Frisia east of the Lauwers is his only from 785. No king is known to have come to Dorestad.
rulers.source: ARF 785, 814; Einhard VK 30; dossier dorestad

rulers.name: Louis the Pious
rulers.title: emperor
rulers.how_ended: died on an island in the Rhine by Ingelheim, 20 June 840
rulers.note: Put down by his sons from June 833 to March 834; the raids on Dorestad begin that summer.
rulers.source: AB 834, 837, 840; dossier noviomagus

rulers.name: Lothar I
rulers.title: emperor; king of the middle kingdom from the treaty of Verdun, August 843
rulers.how_ended: gave up his lands and died a monk at Pruem, 29 September 855
rulers.note: Gave Walcheren to the Dane Harald in 841 and Dorestad to Rorik in 850. Ghent and the land west of the Scheldt went to Charles the Bald in 843, Mainz to Louis the German.

rulers.name: Lothar II
rulers.title: king; his kingdom is the first to be called Lotharingia
rulers.how_ended: died at Piacenza, 8 August 869, leaving no lawful son
rulers.note: His father gave him all Frisia in 855, before he died. In 864 he taxed every manse 4 pennies to hire the Northman Rodulf.
rulers.source: AB 855, 864, 869; wp en Lotharingia

rulers.name: Charles the Bald
rulers.title: king of the West Franks; crowned over Lothar's kingdom at Metz, 9 September 869
rulers.how_ended: at Meerssen, 8 August 870, he left Utrecht and two parts of Frisia to Louis the German and kept one part of Frisia and the land west of the Meuse
rulers.note: Bound Rorik to himself by treaty at Nijmegen in 870. His third of Frisia (taken here as the islands and mouths south of the Maas (?)) stayed West Frankish until 880.

rulers.name: Louis the German
rulers.title: king of the East Franks
rulers.note: Rorik swore to him at Aachen in 873. The men of Oostergo told Rodulf they owed tribute to no one but King Louis and his sons.

rulers.name: Louis the Younger
rulers.title: king of the East Franks
rulers.how_ended: died at Frankfurt, 20 January 882, while his army was out against the Northmen on the Meuse
rulers.note: Beat Charles the Bald at Andernach on the Rhine, 8 October 876. Took the western half of Lotharingia by the treaty of Ribemont, 880.
rulers.source: AF 876, 880, 882; wp en Lotharingia

rulers.name: Charles the Fat
rulers.title: emperor
rulers.how_ended: put down at Tribur, November 887; died 13 January 888
rulers.note: Bought off the Northmen at Asselt in 882 and made Godfrid his man in Frisia; had him killed in 885.

rulers.name: Arnulf of Carinthia
rulers.title: king of the East Franks; emperor from 896
rulers.note: Gave Count Gerulf lands of his own in 889; broke the Northmen on the Dyle by Leuven in 891; set his son Zwentibold over Lotharingia in 895.
rulers.source: AF 891, 899; DD Arnulf (4 August 889), as wp en Gerolf of Holland; Regino 895

rulers.name: Zwentibold
rulers.title: king of Lotharingia under his father Arnulf
rulers.seat: no fixed seat; the Meuse lands
rulers.how_ended: killed in a fight with his own counts on the Meuse, 13 August 900; buried at Susteren
rulers.note: On 24 June 896 he gave the men of Utrecht's church at Deventer and Tiel the freedom they had had at Dorestad.
rulers.source: Regino 895, 900; OSU 88; wp en Zwentibold

rulers.name: Louis the Child
rulers.title: king of the East Franks
rulers.seat: no fixed seat; ruled through bishops and counts
rulers.how_ended: died in September 911 (the day is given as the 20th or 24th (?)), the last of Charlemagne's line in the east
rulers.note: A child of six at his crowning. Duke Gebhard held Lotharingia for him from 903.
rulers.source: Regino 900; wp en Lotharingia

rulers.name: Charles the Simple
rulers.title: king of the West Franks, taken as king by the Lotharingians in 911
rulers.seat: Laon; in Lotharingia often at Herstal and Aachen
rulers.how_ended: seized by Count Herbert of Vermandois in 923 and held till his death in 929; the Lotharingians turned to Henry of the East Franks between 923 and 925
rulers.note: On 15 June 922 at Bladel he gave Count Dirk the church of Egmond and its lands. Frisia east of the Vlie and Mainz stayed with the eastern kings Conrad I (911-918) and Henry I (from 919).
rulers.source: wp en Lotharingia; wp nl Dirk II van Holland (the charter of 922); Flodoard, Annales 923, 925 (?)

rulers.name: Henry I
rulers.title: king of the East Franks
rulers.note: Took Lotharingia in 925 and made Gilbert its duke and his son-in-law in 928. His youngest son Bruno was schooled at Utrecht under Bishop Balderic.
rulers.source: Widukind I.30, I.41 (?); wp en Lotharingia; wp nl Balderik van Utrecht

rulers.name: Otto I
rulers.title: king of the East Franks, crowned at Aachen 7 August 936; emperor from 2 February 962
rulers.seat: Saxony; Aachen, Nijmegen and Cologne on his journeys
rulers.note: Gave the bishop of Utrecht the mint there and the toll at Muiden (953; the mint perhaps in 936); in 948 confirmed Utrecht's rights at 'the estate once called Dorsteti, now Wik'.
rulers.source: Widukind II.1; OSU 111; wp nl Balderik van Utrecht; dossier traiectum

rulers.name: Otto II
rulers.title: emperor
rulers.note: Made Charles, brother of the West Frankish king, duke of Lower Lotharingia in 977.
rulers.source: Thietmar III (?); wp en Lower Lorraine

rulers.name: Otto III
rulers.title: king at three years old; emperor from 996
rulers.seat: Aachen, later Rome; born in the Ketil wood by Nijmegen in 980
rulers.how_ended: died at Paterno near Rome, January 1002 (the 23rd or 24th (?))
rulers.note: His mother Theophanu ruled for him until she died at Nijmegen, 15 June 991. In 985 his charters made Dirk II owner of his fiefs and gave Count Ansfried the king's toll at Medemblik.
rulers.source: Thietmar IV (?); dossier noviomagus; dossier medemelacha

rulers.name: Henry II
rulers.title: king; emperor from 1014
rulers.seat: Bamberg; Nijmegen and Utrecht on his journeys
rulers.note: Brother-in-law of Countess Liutgard of West Frisia. Heard the merchants of Tiel at Nijmegen at Easter 1018 and sent the army that was beaten at Vlaardingen.
rulers.source: Alpert II.20-21; Thietmar (1018); wp nl Slag bij Vlaardingen (1018)

rulers.name: Conrad II
rulers.title: king; emperor from 1027
rulers.seat: Speyer; Nijmegen and Utrecht on his journeys
rulers.how_ended: died at Utrecht at Pentecost, 4 June 1039; his bowels were buried in the cathedral there, his body at Speyer
rulers.note: Gave the bishop of Utrecht the count's rights in Teisterbant, the land of Tiel, in 1026.
rulers.source: Wipo, Gesta Chuonradi 39 (?); dossier traiectum; wp nl Sticht Utrecht

rulers.name: Henry III
rulers.title: king; emperor from 1046
rulers.seat: Goslar; Utrecht and Nijmegen on his journeys
rulers.how_ended: died at Bodfeld in the Harz, 5 October 1056
rulers.note: Went against Count Dirk IV by ship in 1046 and 1047; gave Groningen (1040) and Deventer (1046) to the bishop of Utrecht.
rulers.source: wp nl Dirk IV van Holland; wp nl Sticht Utrecht; dossier daventre

rulers.name: Henry IV
rulers.title: king at six years old
rulers.how_ended: after the game's end (put down by his son in 1105, died 1106)
rulers.note: His mother Agnes ruled for him until April 1062, when Archbishop Anno of Cologne had the boy carried off by ship from Kaiserswerth on the Rhine; then Anno and Adalbert of Bremen ruled. In 1064 his charters gave the county of West Frisia to the bishop of Utrecht.
rulers.source: Lampert of Hersfeld, Annales 1062 (?); wp en William I (bishop of Utrecht)

rulers.name: Gebhard
rulers.title: duke in Lotharingia for Louis the Child
rulers.seat: the Wetterau; no seat in Lotharingia
rulers.source: wp en Lotharingia

rulers.name: Reginar Longneck
rulers.title: count and lay abbot; the first man of Lotharingia, not called duke by the king (?)
rulers.note: Brought down Zwentibold in 900 and led the Lotharingians to Charles the Simple in 911.
rulers.source: Regino 898, 900; wp en Lotharingia

rulers.name: Gilbert (Giselbert)
rulers.title: duke of Lotharingia; from 928 by King Henry's grant, with the king's daughter Gerberga as wife
rulers.how_ended: drowned in the Rhine at Andernach, 2 October 939, fleeing after his rising against Otto I
rulers.source: Widukind II.26 (?); wp en Lotharingia

rulers.name: Henry, brother of Otto I
rulers.title: duke of Lotharingia
rulers.how_ended: driven out by the Lotharingians within the year
rulers.source: wp en Lotharingia

rulers.name: Otto of Verdun
rulers.title: duke of Lotharingia
rulers.source: wp en Lotharingia

rulers.name: Conrad the Red
rulers.title: duke of Lotharingia, son-in-law of Otto I
rulers.how_ended: put out for rebellion in 953; killed at the Lechfeld, 10 August 955
rulers.source: Widukind III (?); wp en Lotharingia

rulers.name: Bruno
rulers.title: archbishop of Cologne and duke of Lotharingia, brother of Otto I
rulers.note: Schooled at Utrecht as a child. In 959 he set Godfrey over the lower half of the duchy and Frederick over the upper; Lower Lotharingia runs from then.
rulers.source: Ruotger, Vita Brunonis (?); wp en Lotharingia; wp nl Balderik van Utrecht

rulers.name: Godfrey I
rulers.title: duke of Lower Lotharingia under Bruno
rulers.how_ended: died in Italy in 964, of sickness in Otto's army (?)
rulers.source: wp en Lower Lorraine

rulers.name: Richar
rulers.title: duke of Lower Lotharingia (?)
rulers.how_ended: died in 972 (?); no duke is named from 964 to 968 or from 972 to 977, and the king held the duchy himself
rulers.source: wp en Lower Lorraine (gives 964-972)

rulers.name: Charles
rulers.title: duke of Lower Lotharingia, brother of King Lothair of the West Franks
rulers.how_ended: taken by treachery at Laon in 991 while claiming the West Frankish crown, and died a prisoner
rulers.source: wp en Lower Lorraine

rulers.name: Otto
rulers.title: duke of Lower Lotharingia, son of Charles
rulers.how_ended: died without a son (the year is given as 1005 to 1012 (?))
rulers.source: wp en Lower Lorraine

rulers.name: Godfrey II of Verdun
rulers.title: duke of Lower Lotharingia
rulers.note: Led the emperor's army against Dirk III in 1018 and was taken at Vlaardingen.
rulers.source: Alpert II.21; wp en Lower Lorraine; wp nl Slag bij Vlaardingen (1018)

rulers.name: Gothelo I
rulers.title: duke of Lower Lotharingia, and of Upper from 1033
rulers.source: wp en Lower Lorraine

rulers.name: Gothelo II
rulers.title: duke of Lower Lotharingia (doubted: the sources call him unfit)
rulers.source: wp en Lower Lorraine

rulers.name: Frederick of Luxembourg
rulers.title: duke of Lower Lotharingia
rulers.note: Set in to keep out Godfrey the Bearded, who rose against Henry III from 1044 to 1049.
rulers.source: wp en Lower Lorraine

rulers.name: Godfrey III the Bearded
rulers.title: duke of Lower Lotharingia
rulers.note: As a rebel he burned the palace at Nijmegen in 1047.
rulers.source: wp en Lower Lorraine; dossier noviomagus

rulers.name: Godfrey IV the Hunchback
rulers.title: duke of Lower Lotharingia
rulers.how_ended: after the game's end: stabbed at Vlaardingen in February 1076 and died at Utrecht (?)
rulers.note: Took West Frisia for the bishop of Utrecht in 1070-1071.
rulers.source: wp en Lower Lorraine; wp nl Floris I van Holland

rulers.name: Gregory
rulers.title: abbot and head of the Utrecht church; never a bishop
rulers.seat: Utrecht, the stone fort and St Martin's
rulers.source: wp nl Lijst van bisschoppen van Utrecht; dossier traiectum

rulers.name: Alberic I
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht
rulers.note: Gregory's nephew and Alcuin's friend; sent Liudger to pull down Frisian shrines.
rulers.source: wp nl Lijst van bisschoppen van Utrecht; dossier traiectum

rulers.name: Theodard
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht
rulers.source: wp nl Lijst van bisschoppen van Utrecht

rulers.name: Hamacar
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht
rulers.how_ended: died in 806; only his name is known
rulers.note: The bishop at the game's start. His church holds a tenth of the king's income at Dorestad and its own plots on the bank there.
rulers.source: wp nl Lijst van bisschoppen van Utrecht; dossier traiectum; OSU 48, 56

rulers.name: Ricfried
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht
rulers.source: wp nl Lijst van bisschoppen van Utrecht

rulers.name: Frederik
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht
rulers.how_ended: stabbed by two men after Mass, between 835 and 838 (his feast is 18 July); held a saint
rulers.note: Preached on Walcheren and sent the canon Odulf to Stavoren. Later writers blame Empress Judith, or men of Walcheren, for his death.
rulers.source: wp nl Lijst van bisschoppen van Utrecht; dossier traiectum

rulers.name: Alberic II
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht
rulers.source: wp nl Lijst van bisschoppen van Utrecht

rulers.name: Eginhard
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht (doubtful)
rulers.source: wp nl Lijst van bisschoppen van Utrecht (about 845, uncertain)

rulers.name: Liudger
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht (doubtful; not the missionary)
rulers.source: wp nl Lijst van bisschoppen van Utrecht (uncertain)

rulers.name: Hunger
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht
rulers.seat: Utrecht until the Northmen sacked it in 857; then St Peter's at Sint-Odilienberg on the Roer, given by Lothar II in 858; at last Deventer
rulers.how_ended: died in exile in 866, at Pruem by one account (?)
rulers.note: Spoke against Lothar II's putting away of his queen. Hincmar of Reims wrote to him in 863 about Rorik's penance.
rulers.source: wp nl Lijst van bisschoppen van Utrecht; dossier traiectum; Flodoard, Historia Remensis ecclesiae III.23 (?)

rulers.name: Odilbald (Adalbold I)
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht in exile
rulers.how_ended: died in 898 or 899; a bishop Alfried is put between Hunger and him by some lists (?)
rulers.note: Utrecht's bank shows flood clay and no houses from about 850 to after 900.
rulers.source: wp nl Lijst van bisschoppen van Utrecht; dossier traiectum; dossier daventre

rulers.name: Egilbold
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht in exile
rulers.source: wp nl Lijst van bisschoppen van Utrecht

rulers.name: Radbod
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht in exile
rulers.how_ended: died at Ootmarsum, 29 November 917; buried at Deventer; held a saint
rulers.note: Of the heathen King Radbod's blood through his mother; bred at Charles the Bald's court; wrote on Lebuin and a poem on a swallow.
rulers.source: wp nl Lijst van bisschoppen van Utrecht; dossier daventre

rulers.name: Balderic
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht
rulers.seat: Deventer, then Utrecht again from about 920
rulers.note: Rebuilt the walls, St Martin's, St Saviour's and the school; won the mint of Utrecht and the toll of Muiden from Otto I.
rulers.source: wp nl Balderik van Utrecht

rulers.name: Folcmar
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht
rulers.source: wp nl Lijst van bisschoppen van Utrecht

rulers.name: Baldwin I
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht
rulers.source: wp nl Lijst van bisschoppen van Utrecht

rulers.name: Ansfried
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht; before that count in Teisterbant and Huy and Otto I's sword-bearer
rulers.seat: Utrecht; in his blindness the abbey of Hohorst (Heiligenberg)
rulers.how_ended: died at Hohorst, 3 May 1010; the Utrecht men carried his body off by boat while the monks fought a fire
rulers.note: With him the king's toll, mint and dues at Medemblik (his since 985) came to the church.
rulers.source: wp nl Ansfried; Alpert I.11-17 (?); dossier medemelacha

rulers.name: Adalbold II
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht; count of Drenthe from 1024 and in Teisterbant from 1026
rulers.note: Complained of Dirk III at Nijmegen in 1018 and fled to the ships at Vlaardingen. Built the new cathedral, hallowed in 1023 before Henry II.
rulers.source: wp nl Sticht Utrecht; wp nl Slag bij Vlaardingen (1018); dossier traiectum

rulers.name: Bernold
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht
rulers.how_ended: died 19 July 1054; buried in his own church of St Peter
rulers.note: Built St Peter's, St John's and St Paul's at Utrecht and the great church at Deventer; got Groningen (1040) and Deventer with its toll and mint (1046) from Henry III.
rulers.source: dossier traiectum; dossier daventre; wp nl Sticht Utrecht

rulers.name: William I
rulers.title: bishop of Utrecht; count of West Frisia by Henry IV's charters of 1064
rulers.how_ended: after the game's end: died in 1076
rulers.note: Went on the great pilgrimage to Jerusalem of 1064-1065.
rulers.source: wp en William I (bishop of Utrecht)

rulers.name: Hildebold
rulers.title: bishop, then archbishop of Cologne (from 794 or 795); the king's chief chaplain
rulers.note: Utrecht answers to Cologne.
rulers.source: wp en List of bishops and archbishops of Cologne (gives 784-818; dates before Gunthar are guesses)

rulers.name: Hadebald
rulers.title: archbishop of Cologne
rulers.note: In 826 he lent Ansgar and the baptised Harald a ship with two cabins for the journey down the Rhine past Dorestad.
rulers.source: Rimbert, Vita Anskarii 7; wp en List of bishops and archbishops of Cologne

rulers.name: Hilduin
rulers.title: holder of the see, never hallowed
rulers.source: wp en List of bishops and archbishops of Cologne

rulers.name: Gunthar
rulers.title: archbishop of Cologne
rulers.how_ended: put out by Pope Nicholas I in 863 for upholding Lothar II's divorce; he clung to the see until a new man was chosen in 870
rulers.source: AB 863-864; wp en List of bishops and archbishops of Cologne

rulers.name: Willibert
rulers.title: archbishop of Cologne
rulers.note: His city was burned by the Northmen in the winter of 881-882.
rulers.source: AF 881; wp en List of bishops and archbishops of Cologne

rulers.name: Hermann I
rulers.title: archbishop of Cologne
rulers.source: wp en List of bishops and archbishops of Cologne

rulers.name: Wichfrid
rulers.title: archbishop of Cologne
rulers.source: wp en List of bishops and archbishops of Cologne

rulers.name: Bruno
rulers.title: archbishop of Cologne and duke of Lotharingia
rulers.note: From his time the archbishop holds court, market, mint and toll at Cologne.
rulers.source: dossier colonia; wp en List of bishops and archbishops of Cologne

rulers.name: Folcmar
rulers.title: archbishop of Cologne
rulers.source: wp en List of bishops and archbishops of Cologne

rulers.name: Gero
rulers.title: archbishop of Cologne
rulers.source: wp en List of bishops and archbishops of Cologne

rulers.name: Warin
rulers.title: archbishop of Cologne
rulers.source: wp en List of bishops and archbishops of Cologne

rulers.name: Everger
rulers.title: archbishop of Cologne
rulers.source: wp en List of bishops and archbishops of Cologne

rulers.name: Heribert
rulers.title: archbishop of Cologne
rulers.note: Between 1016 and 1019 the church and estate of Wijk, old Dorestad, came to him and his abbey of Deutz from Adela of Hamaland.
rulers.source: dossier dorestad; wp en List of bishops and archbishops of Cologne

rulers.name: Pilgrim
rulers.title: archbishop of Cologne
rulers.source: wp en List of bishops and archbishops of Cologne

rulers.name: Hermann II
rulers.title: archbishop of Cologne
rulers.source: wp en List of bishops and archbishops of Cologne

rulers.name: Anno II
rulers.title: archbishop of Cologne; from 1062 the boy king's keeper
rulers.how_ended: after the game's end: died in 1075
rulers.note: One of the lords leagued against Count Floris I in 1058-1061.
rulers.source: wp nl Floris I van Holland; wp en List of bishops and archbishops of Cologne

rulers.name: (no name survives)
rulers.title: the king's agents at Dorestad (procuratores rei publicae), who take his tenth and the bank due
rulers.seat: Dorestad; a lord's enclosed hall stood at De Geer, 500 m from the harbour
rulers.how_ended: the place was given in benefice to two Danes late in Louis the Pious's reign
rulers.note: No count, reeve or tollman of Dorestad is named in any source: 'the count' of the player's debt is a made-up man in a real office.
rulers.source: OSU 56 (charter of 18 March 815); dossier dorestad sections 1 and 8

rulers.name: Harald the Younger, with his brother Rorik
rulers.title: Danish exiles holding the trading place Dorestad in benefice from Emperor Louis
rulers.how_ended: after Louis's death Lothar charged Rorik with treason and held him; he broke out and went to Louis the German. Harald was dead by 850. (The years are guesses: the annal says only 'in Louis's time' and 'after his death') (?)
rulers.source: AF 850; wp en Rorik of Dorestad

rulers.name: (no lord named)
rulers.title: Danes take tribute and hold nearly all the province (846); 'other Danes' hold Dorestad and the Betuwe (847); the counts Sigir and Liuthar fight them
rulers.how_ended: Rorik came with a fleet in 850

rulers.name: Rorik
rulers.title: Northman; the king's man for Dorestad 'and other counties', among them Kennemerland; 'he who is over Dorestad' (857)
rulers.how_ended: last named in 873, swearing to Louis the German at Aachen; dead by 882, when what he had held was given to Godfrid
rulers.note: Lothar I's man 850-855, Lothar II's 855-869, Charles the Bald's from 870, Louis the German's from 873. Driven out by the people called Cokingi in 867, back by 870. Whether he held Utrecht or Medemblik is not said. Baptised by 863.

rulers.name: (no lord named)
rulers.title: Rorik is not heard of after 873; the West Frisians beat a band of Northmen by themselves in 876
rulers.how_ended: the emperor gave the land to Godfrid in 882

rulers.name: Godfrid
rulers.title: Northman king, baptised at Asselt in 882; the emperor's man for Kennemerland and all Rorik had held ('duke of Frisia' is a modern name)
rulers.how_ended: cut down at a parley at Herispich (Spijk, where Rhine and Waal part) in June 885 by Count Everhard and Count Henry's men, on the emperor's word; his men in the Betuwe were killed too
rulers.note: Married Gisela, daughter of Lothar II. In 885 he asked for Koblenz, Andernach, Sinzig and other royal estates, because his own land grew no wine.
rulers.source: AF 882, 883, 885; AB 882; Regino 882, 885; wp nl Godfried de Noorman

rulers.name: Gerulf
rulers.title: count of the Frisians (Regino); count between the Rhine mouth and Suithardeshaga
rulers.note: Carried Godfrid's demand to the emperor in 885 with Count Gardulf. On 4 August 889 King Arnulf gave him as his own a wood and fields between the Old Rhine's mouth and Suithardeshaga, and farms at Tiel, Aalburg and Asch.
rulers.source: Regino 885; wp en Gerolf of Holland

rulers.name: Dirk I
rulers.title: count in Kennemerland
rulers.how_ended: died about 928 or 939; some make two Dirks of him (?)
rulers.note: On 15 June 922 Charles the Simple gave him the church of Egmond and its lands; he set nuns there.
rulers.source: wp nl Dirk II van Holland; wp nl Lijst van graven van Holland (gives c. 916-c. 928)

rulers.name: Dirk II
rulers.title: count in Kennemerland, Maasland and Texel; from 965 also keeper of the fort and county of Ghent
rulers.note: Married Hildegard of Flanders. Built a stone church at Egmond (about 950) and brought monks from Ghent. On 25 August 985 at Nijmegen Otto III made his fiefs his own.
rulers.source: wp nl Dirk II van Holland; dossier witla; dossier medemelacha

rulers.name: Arnulf
rulers.title: count of West Frisia
rulers.how_ended: killed at Winkel, 18 September 993, fighting the West Frisians north of Kennemerland
rulers.source: wp nl Arnulf van Gent

rulers.name: Liutgard of Luxembourg
rulers.title: widow of Arnulf, ruling for her son Dirk III; sister of Henry II's queen
rulers.how_ended: her son came of age about 1005
rulers.note: Held the county only with the king's help. In 1005 Henry II went by ship against the West Frisians for her sake (?).
rulers.source: wp nl Arnulf van Gent; wp en Dirk III, Count of Holland; Thietmar VI (?)

rulers.name: Dirk III
rulers.title: count in Frisia; called 'the Jerusalemite' after a pilgrimage about 1030
rulers.seat: Vlaardingen, a ring fort on the Merwede
rulers.note: Took toll of ships between Tiel and England at Vlaardingen and beat the emperor's army there, 29 July 1018.
rulers.source: Alpert II.20-21; wp en Dirk III, Count of Holland; wp nl Slag bij Vlaardingen (1018)

rulers.name: Dirk IV
rulers.title: count in Frisia
rulers.how_ended: killed at Dordrecht (Thuredrech), 13 January 1049, drawn into a trap by the bishops of Utrecht, Liege and Metz
rulers.source: wp nl Dirk IV van Holland

rulers.name: Floris I
rulers.title: count in Frisia, brother of Dirk IV
rulers.how_ended: killed at Nederhemert, 28 June 1061, taken resting after a won fight
rulers.source: wp nl Floris I van Holland

rulers.name: Dirk V
rulers.title: count in Frisia, a child
rulers.note: His mother Gertrude of Saxony ruled for him; in 1063 she married Robert of Flanders, called the Frisian, who then ruled. From 1064 the bishop of Utrecht had the king's charter for the county; Godfrey the Hunchback took it for him in 1070-1071.
rulers.source: wp nl Floris I van Holland; wp nl Lijst van graven van Holland

rulers.name: Eggihard
rulers.title: count of Walcheren
rulers.how_ended: killed by the Northmen on Walcheren, 17 June 837, with Hemming son of Halfdan; only his death is on record
rulers.source: AF 837

rulers.name: Harald
rulers.title: Danish exile, given Walcheren and the places round it by Lothar
rulers.note: The annalist calls it a hateful thing that Christians should serve men who pray to devils.
rulers.source: AB 841; AF 850; dossier walichrum

rulers.name: Baldwin IV of Flanders
rulers.title: count of Flanders; holds Walcheren of the emperor from 1012 (?)
rulers.note: No lord of the islands is named between 850 and 1012.
rulers.source: dossier walichrum (marked unchecked there)

rulers.name: Baldwin V of Flanders
rulers.title: count of Flanders
rulers.note: Sided with Godfrey the Bearded and Dirk IV against Henry III in 1047.
rulers.source: wp nl Dirk IV van Holland; (?) for the death day

rulers.name: Gerulf the elder
rulers.title: count in Frisia; his lands lay in Westergo (?)
rulers.note: Lost his estates for siding against Louis the Pious and had them back in 839 (?). Thought to be the forefather of the later Gerulf.
rulers.source: wp en Gerolf of Holland (fl. 833, d. 855); the charter of 839 not seen (?)

rulers.name: Albdag
rulers.title: count in Oostergo
rulers.how_ended: named only in 873, when his county killed Rodulf
rulers.source: AF 873; dossier doccinga

rulers.name: Gardulf
rulers.title: count of the Frisians, with Gerulf
rulers.source: Regino 885

rulers.name: Liudolf of Brunswick
rulers.title: count in Frisia (Oostergo, Westergo and Stavoren)
rulers.seat: Brunswick; he and his heirs are not known to have lived in Frisia
rulers.note: The house took the county in 1006 or 1024: the pages differ.
rulers.source: wp nl Brunonen; dossier doccinga

rulers.name: Bruno of Brunswick
rulers.title: count in Frisia
rulers.note: His pennies were struck at Dokkum, Leeuwarden, Bolsward and Stavoren.
rulers.source: wp nl Brunonen; dossier doccinga

rulers.name: Egbert I
rulers.title: count in Frisia; margrave of Meissen from 1067
rulers.note: A charter giving Stavoren its rights in his name is a later forgery.
rulers.source: wp nl Brunonen; wp nl Stavoren

rulers.name: Egbert II
rulers.title: count in Frisia
rulers.how_ended: after the game's end: lost Frisia to the bishop of Utrecht (1086) for rising against Henry IV
rulers.source: wp nl Brunonen; wp nl Sticht Utrecht

rulers.name: Harald Klak
rulers.title: driven-out king of the Danes, baptised 826; given the county of Ruestringen by the Weser as a refuge
rulers.how_ended: killed about 852 by the wardens of the Danish march, who doubted his faith (if this Harald is the same man (?))
rulers.note: Ruestringen lies east of the Ems; Emden's own district, the Emsgau, had Westphalian counts.
rulers.source: ARF 826; AX 826; AF 852; wp en Harald Klak

rulers.name: Hermann
rulers.title: count in the Emsgau (of the house of Werl, or 'of Kalvelage')
rulers.how_ended: not known; his pennies end about 1051
rulers.source: dossier emuthon

rulers.name: Bernhard II of Werl
rulers.title: count in the Emsgau
rulers.how_ended: told in 1062-1063 to hand the county to Archbishop Adalbert of Bremen, and fought it
rulers.source: dossier emuthon

rulers.name: Adalbert, archbishop of Hamburg-Bremen
rulers.title: holder of the Emsgau by the king's gift; of Hunsingo and Fivelgo west of the Ems from 1047-1057
rulers.how_ended: fell from power at court in 1066
rulers.source: dossier emuthon

rulers.name: Everhard Saxo
rulers.title: count in Hamaland
rulers.how_ended: killed in 898 by Waldger, son of Gerulf
rulers.note: By Regino it was an Everhard who struck the first blow at Godfrid in 885, a man whose goods Godfrid had taken.
rulers.source: Regino 885, 898; dossier daventre

rulers.name: Meginhard
rulers.title: count in Hamaland
rulers.source: dossier daventre

rulers.name: Wichman
rulers.title: count in Hamaland; founder of the abbey of Elten
rulers.source: dossier daventre

rulers.name: Adela of Hamaland and her husband Balderic
rulers.title: heiress of Hamaland and the count who claimed the prefect's office
rulers.how_ended: after the killing of Wichman of Vreden in 1016 their fort was taken and they lost all; Adela died after 1021
rulers.note: Pennies in her name were struck at Deventer about 990-1002, with the English king's Hand on one face.
rulers.source: Alpert II; wp nl Alpertus van Metz; dossier daventre

rulers.name: The bishop of Utrecht
rulers.title: count in Hamaland by Henry III's gift of 1046, with Deventer's toll, mint and court
rulers.source: dossier daventre; wp nl Sticht Utrecht

rulers.name: Waldger
rulers.title: count in Teisterbant, son of Gerulf
rulers.note: Had his father's farms at Tiel, Aalburg and Asch. Killed Everhard Saxo in 898.
rulers.source: Regino 898; wp en Gerolf of Holland

rulers.name: Ansfried
rulers.title: count in Teisterbant, Toxandria and Huy; Otto I's sword-bearer
rulers.how_ended: left the world in 994 and was made bishop of Utrecht in 995
rulers.source: wp nl Ansfried

rulers.name: The bishop of Utrecht
rulers.title: holder of the count's rights in Teisterbant by Conrad II's gift of 1026
rulers.note: From now the merchants of Tiel have the bishop for their count.
rulers.source: wp nl Sticht Utrecht

wars.who: Widukind's Saxons and the Frisians as far west as the Vlie, against King Charles
wars.what: The Frisians east of the Vlie threw off the faith, burned the churches and drove out Liudger and the priests. Charles wintered in Saxony; Widukind was baptised in 785 and Frisia to the Weser was Frankish.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: The coast north and east of Dorestad was closed to Frankish ships for two seasons; after 785 a Frisian skipper sails to the Weser under one king and one toll law.

wars.who: Saxons and East Frisians against King Charles
wars.what: A new rising: Count Theoderic's force was wiped out in Ruestringen by the Weser (792 or 793); the East Frisians under Unno and Eilrat burned their churches. Charles marched to the sea at Hadeln in 797 and carried off whole districts of Saxons by 804.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: At the game's start the coast east of the Lauwers is hostile: no safe landing beyond Dokkum, no road east from Deventer. It opens again by stages after 797.

wars.who: Godfred, king of the Danes, against Emperor Charles
wars.what: Godfred burned Reric and moved its merchants to Sliesthorp (808), sent 200 ships to the Frisian islands (810) and boasted he would come to Aachen. He was killed by his own man that year; twelve lords of each side swore peace on the Eider in 811. Charles had a fleet built and guards set at every river mouth.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: The Frisian islands paid 100 pounds of silver. Ship timber and shipwrights were taken for the king's fleet. After 811 the road to Sliesthorp is open and Frisians use it.

wars.who: Emperor Louis the Pious and his sons Lothar, Pippin, Louis and Charles
wars.what: The sons rose in 830 and 833; Louis was put down and set up again (834). After his death the brothers fought at Fontenoy (25 June 841) and shared the empire at Verdun (August 843). Lothar bought Danish help with Walcheren.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: The coast guard stopped working: the first sack of Dorestad came in the summer the emperor was restored. From 843 the Rhine mouths (Lothar), the Scheldt's west bank (Charles) and Mainz (Louis) lie in three kingdoms, each with its own coin and toll.

wars.who: Danish fleets against the Frisian coast and Dorestad
wars.what: Dorestad was plundered four summers running; Antwerp and Witla burned (836); Walcheren was taken and its count killed (837). Louis came to Nijmegen each time too late, blamed the Frisians' disobedience and ordered ships built.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: Tribute, captives and burned storehouses each June. Yet the mint of Dorestad struck more pennies in these years than ever, and no burnt layer has been dug there: the trade went on between the raids. Witla is not heard of again.

wars.who: Danes against Lothar's counts in Frisia; then Rorik against Lothar
wars.what: Three battles in Frisia in 845 (the Northmen lost one and won two); tribute and most of the province in their hands in 846; Dorestad burned under Lothar's eyes; Danes holding Dorestad and the Betuwe in 847. In 850 Rorik came by the Rhine mouths with a fleet, and Lothar, unable to put him out, took his oath and gave him Dorestad.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: From 850 the king's tenth at Dorestad is taken by a Dane in the emperor's name, and his business is to keep other Danes off. Pennies go on being struck in Lothar's name.

wars.who: Rorik and Godfrid Haraldsson in Denmark; other Danes against Dorestad
wars.what: After King Horik fell in the Danes' own war (854), Rorik and Godfrid went home to seek the kingship (855) and came back without it. In 857 Rorik sailed again and held the land between the sea and the Eider for a time; while he was away other Danes stormed Dorestad, plundered the Betuwe and sacked Utrecht.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: A protector who is away is no protector: 857 is the year the bishop left Utrecht for good, and Utrecht's bank lay empty for fifty years.

wars.who: A Danish fleet on the Rhine against Lothar II and the Saxons of Louis the German
wars.what: In January 863, in a winter of great floods, the fleet went up the Rhine, sacked Dorestad, killed Frisian merchants in a large estate where they had fled, burned St Victor's at Xanten and lay on an island by Neuss until about April, with Lothar on one bank and the Saxons on the other. It left on Rorik's advice. In 864 Lothar taxed the land to hire Rodulf, and Northmen went up the Rhine again.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: The last time Dorestad is named as a place worth sacking. Its merchants begin to be found at Deventer, Tiel and on the Rhine above.

wars.who: The Frisians called Cokingi against Rorik; then Charles the Bald and Louis the German over Lothar II's kingdom
wars.what: The people of the land drove Rorik out in 867, and Lothar called up his host for fear he would return with Danes. Lothar died in 869; Charles the Bald had himself crowned at Metz and met Rorik at Nijmegen; at Meerssen (8 August 870) the uncles split the kingdom and Frisia with it.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: The delta changes king twice in a year. From 870 Utrecht, Deventer and two thirds of Frisia are East Frankish; the border with the west runs through the river mouths.

wars.who: Rodulf Haraldsson's fleet against the Frisians of Oostergo
wars.what: In June Rodulf demanded tribute of Oostergo. The Frisians answered that they owed it only to King Louis and his sons, fought, and killed him with 500 or 800 men. The rest, shut in a building, were let go to their ships for their treasure and an oath never to come back, on the counsel of a Northman who had long lived as a Christian among the Frisians.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: Proof that the terp country can defend itself: a good year to be owed money in Oostergo. Raiders avoid the north coast for some years.

wars.who: Charles the Bald against Louis the Younger; West Frisians against Northmen
wars.what: When Louis the German died, Charles the Bald marched on the Rhine to take the rest of Lotharingia and was beaten at Andernach, 8 October 876. The same year the Frisians 'called the Western' beat a band of Northmen and shared out the treasure it had gathered.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: The Rhine above Cologne is a battlefield in harvest time; below it, the West Frisians have silver to spend.

wars.who: The great army of Northmen, come over from England, against the kings of the Franks
wars.what: It wintered at Ghent (879-880), in the palace at Nijmegen (880-881) and at Elsloo on the Meuse (881-882), burning Maastricht, Liege, Tongeren, Cologne, Bonn, Aachen, Pruem and Trier. Charles the Fat besieged its camp at Asselt in July 882, then paid 2,080 or 2,412 pounds of silver and gold, stood godfather to Godfrid and gave him Rorik's lands.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: No ship is safe on the Scheldt, Meuse, Waal or Rhine for three winters. Cologne and Bonn stand burnt; Deventer's port is burned late in 882; the clergy of Cologne flee to Mainz with their relics.

wars.who: Godfrid the Northman as the emperor's man in Frisia; Hugh, son of Lothar II; Count Henry
wars.what: Godfrid let a fleet pass up the Rhine to winter at Duisburg (883-884), married Hugh's sister and plotted with him. In 884 Archbishop Rimbert's Frisians beat a Danish force at Norden. In 885 Godfrid asked for Koblenz, Andernach and Sinzig; he was called to a parley at Herispich and killed, Hugh was blinded, and the fleet Godfrid had called was destroyed in Saxony with the help of Frisians in small boats.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: The end of Danish lordship on the Rhine mouths. A Frisian count, Gerulf, holds the coast from now, and the king rewards him with land of his own (889).

wars.who: King Arnulf against the Northmen on the Dyle
wars.what: After a Frankish army was cut up on the Geul (26 June 891), Arnulf stormed the Northmen's camp at Leuven on foot and filled the river with their dead. The rest raided to Bonn and Pruem in February 892 and then left for England.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: The last great army leaves the Low Countries. No fleet comes up the rivers again until 1006.

wars.who: King Zwentibold against Reginar and the counts of Lotharingia
wars.what: Arnulf's son, set over Lotharingia in 895, fell out with the great men one by one, stripped Reginar in 898 and besieged him in vain. In 898 Waldger, Gerulf's son, killed Count Everhard. The counts killed Zwentibold on the Meuse, 13 August 900.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: The Meuse and Waal are unsafe for a lord's reasons, not a raider's. But it is Zwentibold's charter of 896 that carries Dorestad's old freedom to Deventer and Tiel.

wars.who: The kings of the West and East Franks over Lotharingia
wars.what: The Lotharingians took Charles the Simple as king in 911. Gilbert rose against him; Charles was seized by his own lords in 923; Henry I crossed the Rhine in 923 and 925 and took the whole kingdom.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: For fourteen years Utrecht, Tiel and Nijmegen look to a king at Laon, Mainz and the far coast of Frisia to one in Saxony. From 925 the Rhine from Mainz to the sea has one king, and stays so.

wars.who: Duke Gilbert, Eberhard of Franconia and the king's brother Henry against Otto I
wars.what: The rebels were beaten at Birten by Xanten in March and surprised at Andernach on 2 October 939 as they crossed the Rhine with their plunder. Eberhard was killed and Gilbert drowned.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: Both fights were at Rhine crossings a merchant uses. Count Radbod in Nifterlake, by Utrecht, was among the rebels (?). After it Otto keeps Lotharingia in his own family's hands.

wars.who: Otto I's son Liudolf and Duke Conrad the Red against the king; the Magyars
wars.what: Conrad lost his duchy in 953 and it went to Otto's brother Bruno, archbishop of Cologne. In 954 the Magyars rode through Lotharingia as far as the Meuse and Cambrai. They were destroyed at the Lechfeld in 955.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: Bishop Balderic stood by the king and was paid in trade rights: the mint of Utrecht and the toll of Muiden (953). From now the bishops of Cologne and Utrecht are the lords a merchant deals with.
wars.source: wp nl Balderik van Utrecht; wp en Lotharingia; Flodoard, Annales 954 (?)

wars.who: The counts of West Frisia against the West Frisians north of Kennemerland; King Henry II
wars.what: Count Arnulf was killed at Winkel, 18 September 993, trying to bring the land between the Rekere and the Vlie under him. His widow held on with the king's help; in 1005 Henry II came with ships and made the Frisians yield (?).
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: The inland way north by Medemblik runs through land that owes the count nothing and says so. A West Frisian skipper pays the king's toll at Medemblik, not the count's.
wars.source: wp nl Arnulf van Gent; wp en Dirk III, Count of Holland; Thietmar VI (?)

wars.who: A fleet of Northmen on the Merwede, Waal and Lek
wars.what: In 1006 it came up the Merwede and Waal, plundered and burned the port of Tiel and left before the host gathered. In 1007 it came up the Lek to Utrecht; the people burned their own port and went into the fort, and the Northmen sailed away without an attack.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: Two lost seasons on the river and a burnt waterfront in each of the delta's chief ports. The digs at Tiel show no burnt layer: the merchants rebuilt at once.
wars.source: Alpert I.8-10; wp nl Ansfried; dossier traiectum

wars.who: Count Balderic and Adela of Hamaland against Count Wichman of Vreden and the bishops
wars.what: A feud over the prefect's office on the lower Rhine. Wichman was murdered after a feast in 1016; Balderic's fort at Uflach was taken and burned; he and Adela lost their lands.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: Armed men on both banks between Nijmegen and Deventer for two years. The estate of Wijk, old Dorestad, passes from Adela to the archbishop of Cologne.
wars.source: Alpert II.1-18 (?); wp nl Alpertus van Metz; dossier dorestad

wars.who: Emperor Henry II's army under Duke Godfrey and Bishop Adalbold against Count Dirk III
wars.what: At Easter the merchants of Tiel and the bishop complained at Nijmegen of Dirk's fort and toll at Vlaardingen. A fleet with the men of three bishops landed there on 29 July 1018, was thrown into panic among the ditches and cut down or drowned trying to reach the ships. Godfrey was taken; Adalbold got away by boat.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: The toll stays. Every ship between Tiel or Utrecht and England now pays the count at the river mouth, and the emperor lets it be.
wars.source: Alpert II.20-21; Thietmar (1018); wp nl Slag bij Vlaardingen (1018)

wars.who: Emperor Henry III and the bishops of Utrecht, Liege and Metz against Count Dirk IV; Godfrey the Bearded against the emperor
wars.what: In 1046 the emperor came by ship and made Dirk give back land he had taken about Alphen. In 1047 he took Vlaardingen and Rijnsburg, but lost many men going home through the marsh; Godfrey the Bearded and the counts of Flanders and Hainaut then rose openly and Godfrey burned the palace at Nijmegen. On 13 January 1049 Dirk was trapped and killed at Dordrecht.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: Three years of war at the river mouths, with the Tiel-England road cut whenever a fleet lay at Vlaardingen. Nijmegen's palace is a ruin for a century.
wars.source: wp nl Dirk IV van Holland; dossier noviomagus

wars.who: The bishop of Utrecht, the archbishop of Cologne and their allies against Count Floris I
wars.what: With the empress's leave the bishops made war on Floris. He beat them at Oudheusden in 1061 with pits dug in the field, beat them again at Nederhemert on 28 June, and was killed the same day resting under a tree.
wars.what_it_did_to_trade: The count's toll at the river mouth is in a widow's hands and then in Robert the Frisian's (1063). In 1064 the king gives the whole county to the bishop on parchment; it takes an army to make it true (1070).
wars.source: wp nl Floris I van Holland; wp en William I (bishop of Utrecht)

raids.who: a fleet of 200 ships sent by Godfred, king of the Danes
raids.what: The islands off the coast were laid waste; the Frisians fought three times on the mainland and lost; 100 pounds of silver was paid as tribute.
Men, women and much booty carried off.

raids.who: thirteen pirate ships from the north
raids.what: Driven off by the coast guard with the loss of some cattle and huts; they went on to the Seine and to Bouin.
It laid waste part of Frisia, came by Utrecht to Dorestad and plundered everything; some people were killed, some carried off, and part of the place burned.
It passed by Utrecht on its way to Dorestad; no harm to Utrecht is told.
Dorestad plundered a second time. In Frisia many of the heathen were killed. The emperor set a coast guard.
Antwerp burned.
The trading place Witla at the mouth of the Maas burned; tribute taken from the Frisians. Witla is not named again.
Dorestad and Frisia laid waste a third time. King Horik sent word that it was not his doing.
On 17 June they fell on Walcheren, killed Count Eggihard, Hemming son of Halfdan and many others, led many women away and took what tribute they liked.
From Walcheren they went to Dorestad, laid it waste and took tribute of the Frisians. They left when the emperor reached Nijmegen.
A part of Frisia raided and harmed. King Horik's messengers came with gifts and complaints of the Frisians.
Three battles: the Northmen lost the first and won the other two with great slaughter. The same year a fleet burned Hamburg.
Both districts plundered 'as their custom was'; tribute taken, a battle won, nearly the whole province in their hands.

Dorestad and two other places burned in sight of Emperor Lothar, who was in the fort at Nijmegen and could not punish it. They went home with a great load of people and goods. (The year may be 847: the Fulda annals put the burning there.)

Dorestad and the island of the Betuwe taken and held. Northmen fought the counts Sigir and Liuthar and went nine miles up the Rhine beyond Dorestad to Meinerswijk before turning back with their plunder.

raids.who: Rorik, with a fleet of Danes
raids.what: He came in by the mouths of the Rhine, laid waste Frisia and the Betuwe along the Rhine and Waal, and took Dorestad. Lothar took his oath and let him keep it.
Frisia and the Betuwe laid waste; then on to the Scheldt.
The abbey of St Bavo at Ghent burned.
They took the tribute they asked and went elsewhere. The same year Godfrid, Harald's son, left Lothar, raided Frisia with many ships and went on to the Scheldt and the Seine.

raids.where: the part of Frisia next to Saxony
raids.what: The eastern coast laid waste.

raids.who: 'other Danes', while Rorik was away at the Eider
raids.what: Dorestad stormed and taken; the Betuwe and the lands round it plundered.
Utrecht sacked and its churches wrecked; Bishop Hunger and the clergy fled and did not come back. (The year rests on Lothar II's gift of a refuge in 858.)
raids.source: dossier traiectum; wp nl Lijst van bisschoppen van Utrecht

raids.what: The island between Rhine and Waal raided, and the land beyond the Scheldt.

raids.who: a Danish fleet going up the Rhine towards Cologne
raids.what: In January, with the rivers in flood, Dorestad was sacked. In a large estate where the Frisians had fled many Frisian merchants were killed and many people taken.
The church of St Victor burned; the fleet lay on an island by Neuss until about April, shut in by Lothar and the Saxons, and left on Rorik's advice. More than a hundred raiders were killed.
They went up the Rhine and wasted both banks, Lothar's and Louis's.
A band settled for a time on the IJssel and lived on the land, with Lothar II's leave. The Xanten annals tell of all Frisia being wasted in these years (865-867).

raids.who: Rodulf, Harald's son, nephew of Rorik
raids.what: In June he asked tribute and was refused. He fell with 500 (or 800) of his men; the rest bought their lives with their treasure and swore never to return.
A raid that failed: the West Frisians beat them and shared out the treasure they had taken elsewhere.

raids.who: the great army, come from England
raids.what: It took Ghent in November and wintered there a year, raiding Flanders and the Scheldt.

After burning Birten by Xanten, 'where most of the Frisians live', it walled itself into the king's palace at Nijmegen for the winter. King Louis besieged it in hard frost and got nowhere; in spring the Northmen burned the palace and went down to the Rhine mouths.

raids.who: the great army under Godfrid and Sigfrid, from its camp at Elsloo on the Meuse
raids.what: Cologne and Bonn burned with their churches; Maastricht, Liege, Tongeren, Aachen (the chapel used as a stable), Pruem, Stavelot and Malmedy plundered. The clergy fled to Mainz. Trier was burned on 5 April 882.

raids.who: Northmen, after the peace of Asselt
raids.what: The port 'called Taventeri in the Frisian tongue, where Saint Lebuin rests' was burned and many killed.
They came up the Rhine, burned places newly rebuilt, and wintered at Duisburg. Count Henry drove them off in 884.
A raid that failed: Archbishop Rimbert's Frisians beat them at Norditi in the autumn. A later writer counts 10,377 dead; the treasure taken was kept in common.
raids.source: AF 884; Adam of Bremen I.39 (?); wp en Battle of Norditi

raids.who: Godfrid's own men, and a fleet he had called
raids.what: After Godfrid was killed his men in the Betuwe were cut down. The fleet went on to Saxony and was destroyed there when Frisians of Teisterbant came up behind it in their small boats and took its ships and silver.

raids.who: the remnant of the army beaten at Leuven
raids.what: In February they crossed the Meuse and raided to Bonn and the abbey of Pruem, then left for England.
Stavoren laid waste and other places on the shore lost.
raids.source: Annales Hildesheimenses 991, as wp nl Stavoren

raids.what: They came up the Merwede and the Waal; the people of Tiel fled with what they could carry; the port was plundered and burned, and the church of St Walburg robbed (?). They slipped away before the host could close.

They came up the Lek to Utrecht. The townsmen set fire to their own port so it could not be used against the fort, and went inside the walls. The Northmen said they meant no harm to the holy place, and left.

laws.what: On 8 June King Charles gave St Martin's of Utrecht the church called Upkirika above Dorestad, with land, the bank due on the Lek and the island between Rhine and Lek.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: Part of Dorestad's bank is the bishop's. A man who lands on St Martin's plots pays the church, not the king's agent.

laws.what: King Charles freed the abbey of Saint-Germain-des-Pres of toll at Rouen, Quentovic, Amiens, Maastricht and Dorestad.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: Some ships pass the tollman free by the king's writing. A charter is worth more than a cargo; an abbey's man with one is a rival you cannot undersell.

laws.what: Synod of Frankfurt: the new, heavier penny (about 1.7 g, with the king's monogram) must be taken in every place, town and market; grain and bread have a fixed top price.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: Old light pennies must go to the mint to be struck again, at the king's profit. Refusing a good new penny is an offence. On the far Frisian coast the light weight lingers.
laws.source: Capit. I no. 28 c. 4-5; dossier dorestad

laws.what: Every free man of twelve years and over swears to be true to the emperor.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: A Frisian skipper has sworn too. It is the oath the king's men throw at him when a tribute goes unpaid or a ship is wanted.

laws.what: The law of the Frisians written down for the emperor (about 802). Three Frisias with their own fines: Zwin to Vlie, Vlie to Lauwers, Lauwers to Weser. Four ranks: noble, free, half-free, slave. The law's shilling is 3 new pennies in the middle, 2 and a half in the west, 2 in the east.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: A man carries his own people's law and its prices with him. A free Frisian's life is worth 53 shillings and a penny between Vlie and Lauwers. Blocking the public way on a river costs 12 shillings. Selling a slave to heathen peoples costs your own man-price. Sunday work costs 4 shillings west of the Lauwers and 12 east of it.
laws.source: LF I, XVII, XVIII, Add. III, Add. VI; dossiers doccinga, wijnaldum, emuthon; wp en Lex Frisionum

laws.what: Capitulary of Thionville: only the old, lawful tolls on bridges, ships and markets may be taken; no mail coats or swords may be sold out of the realm.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: A new toll is unlawful and may be refused, if you dare. Frankish blades are the best cargo for the north and the one that costs you everything if the king's men find it.

laws.what: Capitulary of Nijmegen, made in Lent in the palace above the Waal: in the famine oats sell at no more than 2 pennies the measure, barley 3, rye 4, cleaned wheat 6. Buying grain or wine at harvest to sell dear later is shameful gain.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: Buying because you need it is trade; buying cheap to hold for a famine price is a sin with a fine on it. Church treasure may not be bought.

laws.what: The Frisians' duty to the host: counts, the king's men and all who hold horses come themselves; of the poorer men, six fit out a seventh (?).
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: A man with a boat and no horse pays a share of another man's gear and stays at his trade. Loyal Frisians guard their own river mouths.
laws.source: Capit. I no. 48 c. 3 (?); dossier emuthon

laws.what: Capitulary made at Nijmegen: the best double cloak may cost 20 shillings at most, a single one 10; a coat of marten or otter 30. The fine is 40 shillings, half to the man who tells. Only the palace's pennies pass.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: The Frisian's own ware has a ceiling price, and any buyer may turn informer for 20 shillings.

laws.what: The new emperor Louis gave back to the Saxons and Frisians the right to inherit their fathers' land, lost under Charles for their faithlessness.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: In East Frisia a son can again inherit his father's terp and boat without asking the king. A good year to be owed money there.

laws.what: On 18 March Louis confirmed Utrecht's tenth of the king's income and its bank plots 'in Dorestado': St Martin's men on the banks owe the king's agents nothing, no one may be lodged in their houses, and their goods are not seized when they die.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: The dues at Dorestad are the tenth, the bank due and a payment for lodging and safe keeping. To live as St Martin's man is to be free of all three.

laws.what: The old pennies stop passing at Martinmas (11 November); only the new 'Christian religion' penny is good.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: Silver held in old coin must be changed at the mint before the feast, less the moneyer's cut.
laws.source: Capit. I no. 150 c. 20 (?); dossier dorestad

laws.what: The emperor's charter for the merchants of his palace: they go free of toll through the whole empire, except at Quentovic, Dorestad and the Alpine passes, where the tenth is taken for the king. Their ships may not be seized for the king's use, and they come to the palace in mid May.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: Nobody passes Dorestad free: a tenth of the cargo is the king's even from his own men. That tenth is what Rorik, the bishop and later the counts all fight to take.
laws.source: MGH Formulae imperiales no. 37; dossier dorestad

laws.what: The church of Strasbourg's men are freed of toll everywhere in the realm except Quentovic, Dorestad and the passes.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: Rhine wine from Alsace comes down to Dorestad in church ships that pay toll only there.
laws.source: DD Louis the Pious (6 June 831) (?); dossier dorestad

laws.what: After Walcheren the emperor held an inquiry at Nijmegen: the coast guards had failed partly from want of means and partly from the disobedience of some. Abbots and counts were sent to bring the Frisians to heel and a fleet was ordered.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: Ships and men can be called out for the coast watch in the sailing season. The king's men are looking for Frisians to blame.

laws.what: Lothar gave Walcheren and the places round it to the Dane Harald for his help in the brothers' war.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: At the Scheldt mouth the lord is a heathen and his men take what they like from Christians. Pay, or use another mouth.

laws.what: Lothar took Rorik as his man for Dorestad and other counties, on terms: he is to handle the king's dues and all that belongs to the king's purse faithfully, and to keep Danish pirates off.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: The toll is the same tenth, the penny still bears Lothar's name, and the man who takes it is a Dane with ships. It is the best protection on offer, and it works about two years in three.

laws.what: Lothar II took 4 pennies from every manse in his kingdom and paid it, with flour, cattle, wine and cider, to the Northman Rodulf as hire.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: A land tax in coin, the first in living memory: farmers must sell to find 4 pennies, and silver flows to a Danish camp where it can be earned back.

laws.what: Treaty of Meerssen, 8 August: Louis the German takes Utrecht and two parts of Frisia; Charles the Bald takes one part of Frisia and the west bank of the Meuse.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: The river mouths lie on a border. Two kings' tolls and two kings' pennies within a day's sail.

laws.what: Charles the Fat gave the baptised Godfrid the counties and benefices Rorik had held, Kennemerland among them, and paid his fellow king Sigfrid 2,080 pounds (2,412 by another text) out of church treasure.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: A Danish lord at the river mouths again, this time one who lets fleets through. Stay off the Rhine until he is dead.

laws.what: On 4 August King Arnulf gave Count Gerulf, as his own, a wood and fields between the Old Rhine's mouth and Suithardeshaga, and farms at Tiel, Aalburg and Asch in Teisterbant.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: The count on the coast is now a landowner with heirs, not a king's man who can be moved. His sons will be at the river mouth for good.

laws.what: On 24 June King Zwentibold ruled that the men of Utrecht's church at Deventer, Tiel and elsewhere keep the freedom they had 'in Dorestadio': free of the king's toll there.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: Dorestad is gone but its law has moved. The king's toll is now taken at Tiel and Deventer, and the bishop's men pass free.

laws.what: On 1 April Otto I confirmed Utrecht's rights at 'the estate once called Dorsteti, now named Wik'.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: The great port is a farm with a church. Its name is a memory in a charter.

laws.what: Otto I gave Bishop Balderic the mint at Utrecht (some date it 936) and the trading place Muiden on the Vecht with its toll.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: Going north from Utrecht to the Almere you pay the bishop at Muiden. The bishop strikes the pennies you are paid in.
laws.source: wp nl Balderik van Utrecht; dossier traiectum

laws.what: Muiden's toll is given again to the church of Utrecht; by one reading it may now be taken at Utrecht itself, where goods passing must be offered for sale (?).
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: Utrecht becomes a place you cannot sail past: unload, offer, pay.
laws.source: wp nl Sticht Utrecht (975: Muiden); dossier traiectum (marked unchecked there)

laws.what: Otto III, aged five: on 26 June Count Ansfried gets the king's share of toll, mint and dues at Medemblik; on 25 August at Nijmegen Count Dirk II gets his fiefs in Maasland, Kennemerland and Texel as his own.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: The king's tenth on the inland way north is now a count's income, and from 995 the bishop's. The count at the Maas mouth owns his land outright.
laws.source: dossier medemelacha; wp nl Dirk II van Holland

laws.what: The London toll rules (about 1000): the emperor's men who come in their ships are worthy of good laws like the Londoners themselves; at Christmas and Easter they give two grey cloths and one brown, ten pounds of pepper, five pairs of gloves and two casks of vinegar.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: A man of Tiel or Utrecht trades in London on a Londoner's terms, for a fixed gift twice a year. This is the road Dirk's toll sits across.

laws.what: At the Easter court at Nijmegen (6 April) the emperor ordered Count Dirk to stop his toll at Vlaardingen and give back the bishop's land. Dirk refused, won the battle, and kept both.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: An unlawful toll that the emperor cannot lift is a lawful toll. Pay at Vlaardingen.
laws.source: Alpert II.20-21; wp nl Slag bij Vlaardingen (1018)

laws.what: The merchants of Tiel (as Alpert tells it about 1021-1024) judge their own cases by their own will and say the emperor gave them this by charter; they swear each other clear, pool money for common feasts, and drink together on set days.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: A sworn fellowship of merchants: belong to it and your oath is backed by all; stand outside it and you will not win a case at Tiel.

laws.what: The bishop of Utrecht is made count of Drenthe (1024) and holder of the count's rights in Teisterbant (1026).
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: At Tiel the court that hears you is the bishop's. The bishop is now a prince with tolls, mints and soldiers.

laws.what: Henry III gave the king's estate of Groningen to St Martin's of Utrecht.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: A new bishop's market and mint in the north, on the way to the Ems.
laws.source: wp nl Sticht Utrecht; dossier traiectum

laws.what: Henry III gave the bishop of Utrecht Deventer with its toll, mint and court, and the county in Hamaland.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: On the IJssel too the toll is the bishop's. Only the river mouth, the count's, is not.
laws.source: dossier daventre; wp nl Sticht Utrecht

laws.what: The toll list of Koblenz (written into a charter of 1104, thought to be of the mid eleventh century): ships of Tiel, Deventer and Utrecht pay a set due per ship; a ship of Duisburg a cake of wax and a pennyworth of wine; a bought slave 4 pennies; a sword seller every tenth sword.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: The price of going up to the wine country is known before you leave. The tariff is by home port, so it pays to be a man of somewhere.
laws.source: dossier diusburg; dossier daventre (the amount for Tiel, Deventer and Utrecht not seen (?))

laws.what: Henry IV, aged thirteen, gave the bishop of Utrecht the county of West Frisia, the land the counts held at the river mouths.
laws.what_it_means_for_a_merchant: On parchment the bishop takes the toll at Vlaardingen. On the water the count's widow and Robert the Frisian still do, until an army comes in 1070.
laws.source: wp en William I (bishop of Utrecht); wp nl Sticht Utrecht

coins.what: King Charles's first penny, light (about 1.3 g): CARO/LVS in two lines; on the back DOR/STAT and an axe. With Melle, Dorestad is the busiest mint of the kingdom.

The heavy penny (about 1.7 g) with the king's monogram, 240 struck from the pound; it must be taken everywhere from June 794. Foreign coin and old coin are melted and struck again at the king's profit.
coins.source: Capit. I no. 28 c. 5; dossier dorestad; dossier colonia (Cologne's penny of Charles marked unchecked there)

coins.what: The emperor's head on the front; at Dorestad a ship on the back, with DORESTADO or DORESTATVS. Struck for Charles in his last years and for Louis.
Louis's penny with the mint's name written across the back in three lines: DOR/ESTA/TVS.

The 'Christian religion' penny: a cross and the emperor's name; on the back a temple and XPISTIANA RELIGIO, with no mint named. At Dorestad it was struck from some 450 dies: millions of coins. Old pennies stopped passing at Martinmas 825.
Gold: copies of Louis the Pious's gold shilling (MVNVS DIVINVM), made in Frisia through the ninth century and worn as wealth more than spent (?).
coins.source: Grierson 1951, The gold solidus of Louis the Pious and its imitations (from memory, not seen) (?)

coins.what: Lothar's penny of Dorestad: his name as emperor round a cross; on the back the temple and DORESTATVS MON. From about 850 the work is poor: these are most likely Rorik's, struck in the emperor's name.
coins.source: dossier dorestad; wp en Rorik of Dorestad

coins.what: No new royal penny in the delta. Lothar's Dorestad penny is copied on the Frisian coast long after his death (a hoard at Tzummarum in Westergo held 2,600 or more). In Danish hands silver goes by weight: arm rings, bars and Arab dirhams lie with Frankish pennies in the two hoards of Westerklief on Wieringen (about 850 and about 880) (?).
Charles the Bald's penny (GRATIA D-I REX round his monogram), from his new coinage of 864; one mint is Ghent (GANDAVVM). After 870 it is the coin of the western third of Frisia.
coins.source: dossier ganda; Edict of Pitres 864, as chronicle_793.json 864-06-25-pitres

coins.what: The Cologne penny: S / COLONIA / A in three lines, from Louis the Child to Henry II; Otto I's weigh 1.0 to 1.7 g. It is the standard coin of the lower Rhine, and the pennies of the delta copy its stamp.
Utrecht: the mint is the bishop's by Otto I's gift (953, or 936), but the pennies bear the king's name (?).
coins.source: wp nl Balderik van Utrecht; dossier traiectum

coins.what: Deventer: pennies of about 1 g in the names of Otto III and Henry II; the oldest read ODDO REX with DAVNER/A in three lines after Cologne. About 990-1002 some bear Countess Adela's name with the English king Aethelred's Hand; after 1014 the king's mint strikes the Hand type itself. With Tiel it is the chief mint of these lands about 1000, and its coin goes north and east: one lay in a Faroese hoard.

Tiel: the king's pennies with a crowned head and the town's name, of Otto III or Henry II (?) down to Henry III, commonest under Henry II and Conrad II; over 1 g. They turn up in great numbers in the hoards of Scandinavia and the Baltic.
coins.source: dossier emuthon (weight); dossier noviomagus (Tiel's own pennies, 925-1050); types from memory (?)

coins.what: Medemblik: a 'mint' is named in Otto III's charter, but no coin of the place is known before 1280.
Emden: Count Hermann's pennies, HERIMAN and AMVTHON, light (about 0.75 g, the Frisian weight, against over 1 g at Tiel and Deventer).
Bishop Bernold's own pennies, with his name, at Utrecht, at Deventer (from 1046) and at Groningen (from 1040) (?).
coins.source: dossier traiectum (marked unchecked there); dossier daventre

coins.what: The Brunswick counts' Frisian pennies: Bruno's (1038-1057) and Egbert's (1057-1068), about 0.7 g, with the count's name and the place on one face and the king's head on the other (Dokkum: DOCC / BRVN / VGGA). Struck at Dokkum, Leeuwarden, Bolsward and Stavoren; also at Winsum and Garrelsweer. Found from Scandinavia to Russia.
coins.source: dossier doccinga; wp nl Brunonen; wp nl Stavoren

coins.what: Duisburg: the king's pennies of Conrad II, Henry III and Henry IV on the Cologne model; Henry IV's show a church above a wall, seen from the water.

church.what: King Charles gives St Martin's of Utrecht the church above Dorestad, Leusden and four woods; Alberic is made bishop and sends Liudger to pull down the Frisian shrines. Two thirds of the treasure found goes to the king.
In Widukind's rising the Frisians as far as the Vlie drive out the priests and burn the churches. Liudger leaves for Rome and Monte Cassino.

Liudger is given five Frisian districts east of the Lauwers, the Ems mouth among them, to teach. He preaches on the island of the god Fosite, and at Helwerd he gives the blind singer Bernlef his sight.
The East Frisians under Unno and Eilrat burn their churches again; Liudger is back within the year.
Liudger is made the first bishop of Muenster. His five Frisian districts stay under Muenster: the bishop of Utrecht's flock ends at the Lauwers.
Liudger dies at Billerbeck, 26 March.

Harald, driven-out king of the Danes, is baptised at Mainz with his wife and four hundred followers. The monk Ansgar goes north with him in a ship with two cabins lent by the archbishop of Cologne, by way of Dorestad.
Bishop Frederik, who preached against sin on Walcheren and sent the canon Odulf to the Frisians at Stavoren, is stabbed by two men after Mass (835 to 838; his feast is 18 July).

About now Catla of Birka brings her dead mother's silver to Dorestad for alms, as she was told: 'there are many churches, priests and clergy, and a multitude of poor'. Devout women of the place show her where to give.
The Northmen sack Utrecht; the churches are wrecked and Bishop Hunger flees. In 858 Lothar II gives the clergy St Peter's at Sint-Odilienberg; later they settle at Deventer, for sixty years.

Hincmar, archbishop of Reims, writes to Bishop Hunger and to Rorik, 'newly turned to the faith': if Rorik gave the heathen counsel or help in their raid he must do penance, and he must give no shelter to Baldwin of Flanders, who has carried off the king's daughter Judith.
church.source: Flodoard, Historia Remensis ecclesiae III.23, III.26 (?); wp en Rorik of Dorestad

church.what: Godfrid is baptised at Asselt with the emperor as godfather. The same year Northmen burn Deventer, where Saint Lebuin rests.
Rimbert, archbishop of Hamburg-Bremen and Ansgar's pupil, stands with the Frisians at Norden when they beat the Northmen.
Radbod, of the old Frisian king's blood, becomes bishop and rules from Deventer, where he writes of Saint Lebuin and a poem on a swallow. He dies at Ootmarsum in 917.
church.source: dossier daventre; wp nl Lijst van bisschoppen van Utrecht

church.what: Bishop Balderic brings the see back to Utrecht, rebuilds St Martin's, St Saviour's, the school and the walls, and brings relics of Agnes and Pontian from Rome and Odulf's bones to St Saviour's.
church.source: wp nl Balderik van Utrecht; dossier traiectum

church.what: Count Dirk receives the church of Egmond, where Saint Adalbert lies, and sets a house of nuns there.
church.source: wp nl Dirk II van Holland

church.what: Dirk II and Hildegard build a stone church at Egmond (about 950) and bring monks from Ghent; about 975 they give it a gospel book.
church.source: wp nl Dirk II van Holland

church.what: Bruno, once a schoolboy at Utrecht, becomes archbishop of Cologne and duke of Lotharingia at once: the first bishop to rule a duchy.
church.source: wp en Lotharingia; wp nl Balderik van Utrecht

church.what: Count Ansfried lays his sword on the altar at Aachen and is made bishop of Utrecht. He founds the abbey of Hohorst (about 1006), goes blind, and dies there in 1010.
Fire takes Utrecht's cathedral and the bishop's house. Adalbold's new cathedral is hallowed in 1023 before Emperor Henry II and twelve bishops.
Raiders steal Saint Odulf's bones from Stavoren; a bishop buys them in London for the abbey of Evesham.

Emperor Conrad II dies at Utrecht at Pentecost; his bowels are buried in the cathedral. Bishop Bernold builds St Peter's (hallowed 1048), St John's and the abbey of St Paul (1050) round it, and a great church at Deventer.
Bishop William leaves with the great company of pilgrims for Jerusalem; he is back in 1065.
church.source: wp en William I (bishop of Utrecht)

do_not_claim: No count, reeve, tollman or moneyer of Dorestad is named in any source of 793. The office is real; the man is invented.
Charlemagne's charter of Frisian freedom is a forgery of the 13th century. Before 1066 the Frisians have counts and pay the king's dues.
'Duke of Frisia' for Godfrid, 'county of Holland' and 'count of Holland' are later names: until about 1100 they are counts in Frisia or West Frisia.
Rorik of Dorestad is not shown to be the Rurik of Ladoga and Novgorod.
The 'Rorik' who fasts from meat and mead in the Xanten annals for 845 is King Horik of the Danes.
No burnt layer was found at Dorestad or at Tiel: the annals' 'destroyed everything' is a monk's phrase.
No source says Rorik held Utrecht, Medemblik, the Maas mouth or Westergo by name: only 'Dorestad and other counties' and Kennemerland.
Tiel's merchants are not called a guild by Alpert; he describes sworn men who feast from a common purse.
needs: ports_793.json has no Tiel (Tiele, 51.89 N 5.43 E, on the Waal: the delta's chief port about 890-1050), no Stavoren (Staveren, 52.88 N 5.36 E, 9th-11th century), no Vlaardingen (Flardinga, 51.91 N 4.34 E, the count's toll from about 1015) and no Dordrecht (Thuredrech, 1049). Raids, laws and coins here name them in words.
ports_793.json ends Dorestad in 863; the harbour was in use to about 875 and Rorik was its lord to 873.

A realm id for the game's later years: the ports here are all 'franks'. After 843 they are Lothar's, after 870 East Frankish (with a western third), after 925 the East Frankish kingdom and then the Empire.
